title: Keep every list price the ERP ever had

ticket.subject: We lose the old list prices every week
body: The ERP export replaces `erp_products` in the landing schema every week, so the warehouse only ever knows
today's list price. We need the history: which price a product had before a markdown, and when it changed.
Can you keep every version of each product (name, subcategory, list price) with the period it was valid?
Two things we already know about this export:
- every row gets the new `loaded_at` each week, even when nothing about the product changed;
- a discontinued product simply stops being exported. We still want its history, but it must no longer
show up as a current product.
This week's export is already in the landing schema. Once your history is in place, load next week's export
with **Load next batch** and run the project again the way the nightly job would.

acceptance.text: A snapshot snp_erp__products tracks the ERP products by product_id.
After next week's run, a product has a new version only when its name, subcategory or price changed.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS versions, count(DISTINCT product_id) AS products FROM dbt_dev_snap.snp_erp__products
checks.fail: The snapshot does not hold one version per real change.

acceptance.text: Both markdowns keep the old price in a closed version and the new price in the current one.

checks.sql: SELECT product_id, CAST(list_price AS DOUBLE) AS list_price, CASE WHEN dbt_valid_to IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_current FROM dbt_dev_snap.snp_erp__products WHERE product_id IN ('P02', 'P07')
checks.fail: A marked-down product does not show its old and new price as expected.

acceptance.text: The discontinued trekking poles keep its history but has no current version.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS versions, count(*) FILTER (WHERE dbt_valid_to IS NULL) AS current_versions FROM dbt_dev_snap.snp_erp__products WHERE product_id = 'P10'
checks.fail: The discontinued product is missing, or still shows up as current.

acceptance.text: Your last dbt command ran the snapshot, and everything passed.

requires.message: Next week's export has not landed yet: click Load next batch, then run dbt again.

check.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM snap_raw.erp_products WHERE product_id = 'P09'

hints: A table that only ever holds the latest export needs something that remembers the previous rows: that is what a dbt snapshot does.
Since dbt Core 1.9 a snapshot can be declared in YAML under snapshots/, with `relation: source(...)` and a `config` block.
The timestamp strategy trusts `updated_at` to change only when the row changes. Does `loaded_at` behave like that here?
The check strategy compares the columns you list in `check_cols`; `all` would include `loaded_at` too. Look at `hard_deletes` for products that disappear.
